page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across several standard workloads, alongside notable limitations in multi-core scaling. The instance achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core tests, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput. However, multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests falls into the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is average, but large-block memory write bandwidth is weak. Cryptographic and database operations also rank in the lower quartile, and LLM inference speeds for medium 7B models are poor, processing only 5.29 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.cm4.2xlarge offers dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, which ensures consistent compute allocation but limits parallel thread density compared to newer architectures. Given the lack of local storage and the moderate 3 Gbps network baseline, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as light web serving, basic Redis caching, and single-threaded or moderately threaded application servers that do not require high-speed local disk I/O or intensive multi-core parallel processing.
